chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever prays the obligatory prayers at the beginning of their time and fulfills their rites, the angel raises them to heaven white and pure, and they chant to him: 'May God preserve you just as you preserved me, and may God entrust you just as you entrusted me to a noble angel.' And whoever prays them after their time without an excuse and does not fulfill their rites, the angel raises them black and dark, and they chant to him: 'You have wasted me! May God waste you just as you wasted me, and may God not take care of you just as you did not take care of me.'

Then al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the first thing the servant will be asked about when he stands before God, exalted is His majesty, is the obligatory prayers, and about the obligatory zakat, and about the obligatory fasting, and about the obligatory Hajj, and about our wilaya, the Ahl al-Bayt. If he proclaims our wilaya and then dies upon it, his prayers, his fasts, his zakat, and his Hajj will be accepted from him. But if he does not proclaim our wilaya before God, exalted is His majesty, God the Mighty and Majestic will not accept anything from his deeds.

key_terms.الصلوات المفروضات: The five obligatory daily prayers prescribed by God
key_terms.حدودها: The rites, conditions, and proper manner of performing prayer
key_terms.ولايتنا أهل البيت: The wilaya (spiritual authority/guardianship) of the Prophet's household

ai.seo_question: What are the five things a person will be asked about on the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes how obligatory prayers performed on time ascend to heaven in radiant form, praising the worshiper, while neglected prayers ascend in darkness, cursing the one who neglected them. He then explains that the five things a servant will first be questioned about on the Day of Judgment are: the obligatory prayers, zakat, fasting, Hajj, and the wilaya of the Ahl al-Bayt -- with the acceptance of all other deeds contingent upon acknowledging this wilaya. This teaching, delivered in the 4th-century Hijri scholarly circles of Qom, underscores the Shia creedal position that adherence to the Imamate is the condition for the validity of all worship.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Hisham b. Salim from `Ammar b. Musa al-Sabati from Abi `Abdillah Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Sadiq (as). He said:

When one prays the obligatory prayers at the beginning of their timings, fulfilling their rites, the angel takes them up to heaven in a pure, bright form. They will chant: “May Allah preserve you just as you preserved me. May Allah safeguard you just as you safeguarded me with a noble angel.” When one prays it after its timing for no reason and does not fulfill its rites, the angel takes it up in a dark, shadowed form. It will chant: “You have lost me. May Allah lose you just as you lost me. May Allah not take care of you just as you did not take care of me.”

Then, al-Sadiq (as) said: The first things that the worshiper will be asked about when he stands before Allah are the obligatory prayers, the obligatory zakat, the obligatory fasting, the obligatory Hajj, and the wilaya of us, the Ahl al-Bayt. If he proclaims the wilaya and then dies upon it, his prayers, his fasts, his zakat, and his Hajj will be accepted from him. However, if he does not proclaim our wilaya before Allah, then Allah will not accept anything of his deeds.
